title.en: Have and have got: I've got a cat

rule.en:
**have** is for what you own or hold: **I have**, **you have**, **we have**, **they have**, but **he / she / it has**: **Jack has a dog.**

In British English, **have got** is just as common in everyday speech and means the same: **I've got a black cat.** **She's got two brothers.**

Questions and negatives are different for each. With **have**, use do / does: **Do you have a pencil?** **I don't have a bike.** **Does she have a cat?** With **have got**, have itself moves: **Have you got a pencil?** **I haven't got a bike.** **Has she got a cat?** Never mix them (not *Do you have got*).

Only **have** (never have got) is for actions: **have breakfast**, **have lunch**, **have a shower**, **have fun**. These can take -ing too: **We're having lunch.**

The past is **had** for both: **I had a cat.**

Age and feelings take be, not have: **I'm ten.** **I'm hungry.**
rule.sl:
**have** (imeti) je za to, kar imamo: **I have**, **you have**, **we have**, **they have**, pri **he / she / it** pa **has**: **Jack has a dog.** (Jack ima psa.)

V britanski angleščini je v vsakdanjem govoru prav tako pogost **have got**, pomen je enak: **I've got a black cat.** (Imam črno mačko.) **She's got two brothers.**

Vprašanje in zanikanje sta pri vsakem drugačna. Pri **have** rabimo do / does: **Do you have a pencil?** (Imaš svinčnik?) **I don't have a bike.** **Does she have a cat?** Pri **have got** se premakne sam have: **Have you got a pencil?** **I haven't got a bike.** **Has she got a cat?** Ne mešaj ju (ne *Do you have got*).

Samo **have** (nikoli have got) je za dejanja: **have breakfast** (zajtrkovati), **have lunch** (kositi), **have a shower** (tuširati se), **have fun** (zabavati se). Ta so lahko tudi z -ing: **We're having lunch.** (Kosimo.)

Preteklik je za oba **had**: **I had a cat.**

Starost in počutje gresta z be, ne s have: **I'm ten.** **I'm hungry.**
rule.it:
**have** (avere) indica ciò che si possiede: **I have**, **you have**, **we have**, **they have**, ma con **he / she / it** diventa **has**: **Jack has a dog.** (Jack ha un cane.)

Nell'inglese britannico parlato è altrettanto comune **have got**, con lo stesso significato: **I've got a black cat.** (Ho un gatto nero.) **She's got two brothers.**

Domande e negazioni sono diverse per i due. Con **have** servono do / does: **Do you have a pencil?** (Hai una matita?) **I don't have a bike.** **Does she have a cat?** Con **have got** si sposta have stesso: **Have you got a pencil?** **I haven't got a bike.** **Has she got a cat?** Non mescolarli (mai *Do you have got*).

Solo **have** (mai have got) si usa per le azioni, dove l'italiano dice spesso fare: **have breakfast** (fare colazione), **have lunch** (pranzare), **have a shower** (fare la doccia), **have fun** (divertirsi). Qui va anche la forma in -ing: **We're having lunch.**

Il passato è **had** per tutti e due: **I had a cat.**

L'età e le sensazioni vogliono be, non have: **I'm ten.** **I'm hungry.** (Ho fame.)
rule.de:
**have** (haben) steht für Besitz: **I have**, **you have**, **we have**, **they have**, aber bei **he / she / it** heißt es **has**: **Jack has a dog.** (Jack hat einen Hund.)

Im britischen Alltag ist **have got** genauso häufig und bedeutet dasselbe: **I've got a black cat.** (Ich habe eine schwarze Katze.) **She's got two brothers.**

Frage und Verneinung sind bei beiden verschieden. Bei **have** braucht man do / does: **Do you have a pencil?** (Hast du einen Bleistift?) **I don't have a bike.** **Does she have a cat?** Bei **have got** rückt have selbst nach vorn: **Have you got a pencil?** **I haven't got a bike.** **Has she got a cat?** Nie mischen (nicht *Do you have got*).

Nur **have** (nie have got) steht für Handlungen: **have breakfast** (frühstücken), **have lunch** (zu Mittag essen), **have a shower** (duschen), **have fun** (Spaß haben). Hier geht auch die -ing-Form: **We're having lunch.**

Die Vergangenheit ist bei beiden **had**: **I had a cat.**

Alter und Befinden stehen mit be, nicht mit have: **I'm ten.** **I'm hungry.** (Ich habe Hunger.)

examples.en: Shepherd Jack has got a sheepdog called Meg.
examples.sl: Pastir Jack ima ovčarsko psičko Meg.
examples.it: Il pastore Jack ha un cane da pastore che si chiama Meg.
examples.de: Schäfer Jack hat eine Hütehündin namens Meg.

examples.en: Have you got a pencil, Harry? — Yes, I have.
examples.it: Hai una matita, Harry? — Sì, ce l'ho.
examples.de: Hast du einen Bleistift, Harry? — Ja, hab ich.

note.en: With have got, have moves to the front; the short answer is Yes, I have.
note.sl: Pri have got gre have na začetek; kratki odgovor je Yes, I have.
note.it: Con have got, have va all'inizio; la risposta breve è Yes, I have.
note.de: Bei have got rückt have nach vorn; die Kurzantwort ist Yes, I have.

examples.en: Excuse me, do you have any heather honey?
examples.it: Scusi, ha del miele di erica?

note.en: With have, the question takes do: Do you have …?
note.sl: Pri have vprašanje dobi do: Do you have …?
note.it: Con have la domanda prende do: Do you have …?
note.de: Bei have braucht die Frage do: Do you have …?

note.en: doesn't have, not doesn't has: after does comes the base form.
note.sl: doesn't have, ne doesn't has: za does pride osnovna oblika.
note.it: doesn't have, non doesn't has: dopo does va la forma base.
note.de: doesn't have, nicht doesn't has: nach does kommt die Grundform.

note.en: An action: have breakfast, never have got breakfast.
note.sl: Dejanje: have breakfast, nikoli have got breakfast.
note.it: Un'azione: have breakfast, mai have got breakfast.
note.de: Eine Handlung: have breakfast, nie have got breakfast.

examples.en: Mr Dixon hasn't got a horse, he's got two ponies.
examples.sl: Gospod Dixon nima konja, ima dva ponija.
examples.it: Il signor Dixon non ha un cavallo, ha due pony.
examples.de: Herr Dixon hat kein Pferd, er hat zwei Ponys.

examples.en: We're having a picnic by the tarn.
examples.it: Facciamo un picnic vicino al laghetto.
examples.de: Wir machen ein Picknick am Bergsee.
